title: Route latency chronicle: streaming vs non-streaming epoch and percentile breakdowns
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Build a comprehensive dashboard and supporting telemetry to show latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) for every model route, with explicit breakdowns for streaming vs non-streaming IO modes and epoch/time-sliced views. This ticket covers the tracing hooks changes to propagate route/model metadata, histogram and summary metric emission in the backend, metric pipeline (Prometheus/ClickHouse ingestion and retention), log enrichment keys for trace linking, and the final dashboard panels and SLI definitions. The aim is to enable engineers and SREs to quickly identify whether tail latency regressions are caused by streaming codepaths, model variant changes, or infra/memory pressure. Focus on low-cardinality baseline metrics with accompanying high-cardinality sampling for drill-down.
acceptance_criteria: Trace enrichment: every request trace contains route_id, model_id, io_mode (streaming|non-streaming), shard_id, and request_shape tags
Metric emission: backend emits latency histograms with predefined buckets and summary metrics for p50/p95/p99 per (route, model, io_mode) on the 1m and 5m rollups
Pipeline: metrics are ingested into ClickHouse and Prometheus and available via the query layer within 2 minutes

Dashboards: new latency board with: overview heatmap (routes x models), streaming vs non-streaming toggle, epoch selector (last 1h/6h/24h/7d), percentile sparklines, waterfall decomposition for selected route
Drilldown: clicking a cell opens trace search filtered by the triangle (route, model, io_mode) and pre-populates a trace-time range covering the percentile window
SLIs: define and register SLI templates for route-level p95 and p99 for both IO modes and attach to alert rules
Runbook: add short remediation steps and common root causes to the dashboard help panel
tasks: Add trace hook changes: attach route_id/model_id/io_mode at the gateway and proxy layers
Implement histogram buckets in runtime (consider HDR vs fixed buckets) and emit via statsd/metrics client
Create ClickHouse materialized view for aggregated percentiles and 1m/5m rollups
Add log enrichment keys and ensure consistent request_id for trace -> log joins
Design dashboard layout and wireframes in Figma (link to design asset)
Implement Grafana panels and the interactive drilldown link to trace UI
Add SLI definitions and connect to pager/alerting with sensible thresholds
Run an A/B test enabling high-cardinality metrics sampling for 10% of traffic and validate cost impact
notes: We need to balance cardinality (route+model+io_mode) against backend storage and query cost. Proposed approach: emit low-cardinality aggregated histograms every minute for all routes, while sampling detailed per-request histograms/traces at 1% by default with a feature flag to increase sampling for specific customers.
implementation_decisions: Use fixed histogram buckets aligned across runtime and pipeline to avoid bucket mismatch and allow efficient rollups
Store pre-aggregated percentile materialized views in ClickHouse for cheap queries; compute raw percentiles on-demand for drilldown via sampled data
Route metadata tags will be strings limited to 64 chars; canonicalize model_id and route_id at ingress to control cardinality
queries_and_panels: Overview heatmap: SELECT model_id, route_id, quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) FROM metrics.latency_histogram WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1h GROUP BY model_id, route_id
Streaming vs non-streaming: GROUP BY io_mode and plot p50/p95/p99 lines with 1m resolution
Percentile sparkline: use materialized percentiles table with lookback window and overlay deploy markers
Waterfall: decompose average latency into (ingress, routing, model_infer, serialization, network) using tagged spans from traces
